The remark makes three assertions and the record's own gap field concedes that all three are unformalized: (1) representable functors preserve all limits -- 'nowhere asserted'; (2) U : Grp ⟶ Sets preserves all limits -- no Grp exists; (3) faithfulness of the representable is the precise form of Grp's concreteness -- no definition of concrete category, and no functor in the tree is ever exhibited as representable. The sole evidence offered, ev1_Faithful (Theory/Lawvere/Sets.v:105, verified verbatim, under the reachability hypothesis at :101), is faithfulness of an EVALUATION functor on models of an arbitrary Lawvere theory: a different category, a different functor, and a functor never shown representable. That is an analogue of the concreteness PHENOMENON, not a partial formalization of any clause of this item, so under the frozen definition ('PARTIAL = some of the item exists') the record is ABSENT. Contrast awodey:7.1:example2, which I left at PARTIAL because its evidence (EnrichedFunctor_Two_monotone) is the same claim in a different presentation rather than a different claim. I independently re-verified the negative side: PreservesLimit (Structure/Limit/Preservation.v:48) is inhabited only at Adjunction/Continuity.v:202 (right adjoints) and Theory/Equivalence/Limit.v:421 (equivalences); Hom(A,-) is never shown continuous or a right adjoint; rg 'Complete|Limit' over Instance/Sets.v and Instance/Sets/*.v yields one prose hit only.
